Arusuvai

Your Recipe Companion — a local-first, standalone recipe book for keeping recipes, bilingual ingredients, cooking instructions and beautiful exportable recipe cards together.

What Arusuvai does

Arusuvai is designed as a personal digital recipe book: recipes remain available in the browser, can be searched across recipe names and ingredients, and can be edited, favorited, duplicated and exported as complete recipe cards.

The app is built to work locally first. Google Drive is an optional backup/sync path rather than a requirement for normal recipe use.

Core features

📖 Complete recipe cardsRecipe identity, description, toolkit/profile, ingredients, cooking timeline, notes and cheat sheet stay together.
♥ Favorites & recent recipesMark recipes as favorites and quickly return to recipes you recently opened.
🔎 Multi-language searchSearch recipe names, local-language names, ingredients, aliases, cuisine, taste, Recipe No. and Culinary Dictionary terms.
📚 Culinary DictionaryMaintain reusable English/local-language terms, aliases and categories for better ingredient discovery and search.
✏️ Recipe builderCreate and edit recipes with ingredients, grouped sections, timed cooking phases, equipment, profile, cheat sheet and notes.
🌗 Light & dark themesSwitch themes from the top bar. Recipe viewing and exports use the active theme.
🖼 High-resolution PNG exportExport the complete recipe card as a full-card PNG at 3× rendering resolution for sharp sharing and printing.
🖨 Print / Save as PDFPrint the complete recipe card using the same export layout. Browser print can be used to save a PDF.
🍲 Recipe image watermarkExport/print can place the recipe artwork behind the card at low opacity. The watermark option is checked by default.
💾 JSON backup & restoreBack up App Settings, Recipes, Culinary Dictionary or All Data. Favorites and Recent Recipes can be included.
🔄 Merge or replace importImported JSON backups are identified by type before you choose whether to merge or replace the matching local data.
☁️ Google Drive syncOptionally sync selected Arusuvai JSON data to your own Google Drive, including local/Drive restore and merge choices.

Exporting a recipe

From a recipe, use the image or print action and choose whether to use the recipe artwork as a background watermark. The watermark is intentionally subtle so the recipe remains readable while the artwork provides a visual identity.

Recipe image ON → theme base + low-opacity recipe artwork + recipe card Recipe image OFF → clean active-theme recipe card PNG → full card rendered at 3× resolution PDF → browser Print / Save as PDF using the export layout

Backup & restore

  • App Settings — display/search settings, theme and related app configuration.
  • Recipes — recipe records, favorites and recent-recipe information.
  • Culinary Dictionary — dictionary entries and categories.
  • All Data — the complete Arusuvai data set in one JSON backup.
  • Import supports Merge or Replace for the matching backup type.

Recipe artwork used by the built-in/default recipes is part of the app and does not need to be separately restored from JSON.

Google Drive sync

Drive sync is optional. You choose which Arusuvai data types to sync, and the app uses the same JSON backup structure for Drive storage.

  • Connect your Google account from Settings → Data Backup.
  • Choose App Settings, Recipes, Culinary Dictionary or All Data.
  • If data exists on both sides, Arusuvai lets you keep local data, keep Drive data, or merge.
  • A Google OAuth Client ID is required for the current hosted deployment configuration.

Data & privacy

Core recipe data is stored locally in your browser on the device where you use Arusuvai. Normal recipe browsing, editing, searching and local backup do not require a server.

Google Drive is different: when you explicitly connect it, selected backup data is sent to your own Google Drive through Google's APIs. Keep a JSON backup before clearing browser data or changing devices.

Sharing / deployment

Arusuvai is packaged as a standalone HTML application and can be hosted from a static site such as GitHub Pages. The service worker, manifest, icons and supporting legal/documentation files can be added alongside this HTML for the installable PWA deployment.

If you deploy your own copy and use Google Drive sync, configure the OAuth client for your own deployment rather than reusing credentials belonging to another deployment.
